title: Communist Laos

endonym.native: ສາທາລະນະລັດ ປະຊາທິປະໄຕ ປະຊາຊົນລາວ

capsule: The Lao People's Democratic Republic (ສາທາລະນະລັດ ປະຊາທິປະໄຕ ປະຊາຊົນລາວ) was proclaimed on 2 December 1975 after the Pathet Lao, backed by North Vietnam, forced King Savang Vatthana's abdication, ending the Royal Lao government. The ruling Lao People's Revolutionary Party has maintained a single-party state modelled on Vietnamese communism, initially pursuing collectivization that was largely abandoned by the 1980s in favour of market-oriented reforms (Chin Thanakan Mai) similar to Vietnam's Doi Moi. Since the 1990s Laos has pursued regional integration through ASEAN membership (1997) and hydropower development on the Mekong, becoming a significant electricity exporter to Thailand and China.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Boundaries are defined by French colonial delimitation and post-1954 treaties; the border with Vietnam in the eastern Annamite Range has been demarcated in detail.
